notes:
Inbound SMB lead — came through marketing landing page offering 'summarize tickets + structured metadata'. Customer builds a lightweight helpdesk automation layer that plugs into Zendesk/Freshdesk. Wants a hosted/self-serve path (low friction) to evaluate. Key asks: 
- Structured output: map extracted fields to ticket fields (priority, category, product_tag). Wants deterministic JSON schema output for downstream ingestion.
- Tool calling: ability to call webhooks or custom connectors to create/update tickets in partner systems (webhook auth, idempotency).
- Ticket summarization: concise agent-ready summaries (1-3 sentences) + bullets for root cause and recommended next steps.
- Latency expectations: p95 < 300ms for single-turn agent prompt; ok with slightly higher for long-context summarization but prefer <1s.
- Throughput: early POC ~50 concurrent sessions, scale plan to 200 concurrent sessions in Q3 if adoption.
- Cost sensitivity: startup budget, wants recommendations for model selection and batching to reduce token spend. Mentioned preference toward open models / quantized variants if quality holds.
- Security: requires SSO for their admin console (SAML), audit logs and ability to supply KMS for encrypting customer data in transit/at rest. Not asking for full data residency yet, prefer hosted in NA.

Call notes (Avery):
- "We need reliable JSON output so our mapping layer isn't doing NLP heuristics" — VP Product (Lena).
- Engineering will do 2-week POC, must include sample live tool-calls to their staging Zendesk.
- Legal: wants retention policy + incident response info before enabling sandbox keys.

POC success criteria (from demo):
- 95% of automated summaries align with human baseline for S1 tickets on Jaccard score threshold (internal).
- Structured payload matches ticket schema fields without manual patching > 90% of the time.
- Roundtrip tool-calling in staging completes without duplicate tickets and includes idempotency token support.
